thread:
jamal_ops: Quick heads-up — scheduling a rolling reboot for aurora-gpu pool in apac-south tomorrow 02:00-05:00 UTC to apply nvme + driver fixes. Will do cohort-based drains (8 racks, ~6 nodes each), not a full pool drain.

maria_infra: ETA and impact? any tenant-level SLAs to call out?

jamal_ops: ETA 02:00 start. We expect ~2-3 racks down at a time, each rack ~10-15% of apac capacity. Pod eviction target 90s drain + 5m post-drain soak. No planned user-facing outage; latency SLOs might see short spikes.

alex_s: Suggest we pin heavy batch workloads off the pool during window. Can we shift some capacity to eu-west temporarily?

maria_infra: We can pre-warm eu-west burst pool but cost spike ~+12% for the night. Ops: are you ok with that tradeoff?

jamal_ops: Budget OK for this one-off. Prefer preventing tail latency >250ms. We'll only route critical realtime routes away; best-effort batch can queue.

ops-bot: @here Maintenance scheduled: aurora-gpu rolling reboot, 2026-03-22 02:00-05:00 UTC. Affected: apac-south GPU pool. See runbook: https://intra/redwood/ops/aurora-maint.

sophia_oncall: Do we have an automated fallback policy if a cohort reboot takes longer? i.e., auto-shift to dedicated-capacity?

jamal_ops: Yes — routing policy will automatically fallback to dedicated-capacity tier for chat endpoints when node_avail < 70% for >5m. We'll keep on-call in loop for manual override.

ton y_net: Network note: NIC microcode requires a soft reset after driver update; there is a risk of brief ARP flaps per rack. Plan to stagger NIC resets by 3m between racks to reduce convergence load.

alex_s: Can you paste the drain command being used? wanna make sure controller labels preserved for KV caches.

jamal_ops: Using our standard command:

```
./robinctl drain --pool aurora-gpu --rack $RACK --grace 90 --preserve-labels kv-cache=true --soak 300
```

maria_infra: Important: preserve-labels flag prevents KV cache invalidation. If any node gets `oom-kill` during reboot, alert severity = high.

ops-bot: Preflight checks passed (disk health, temp sensors, latest bootloader). Canary cohort = rack-03. Canary start 02:00, observe 10m.

sophia_oncall: I'll watch latency dashboards and token-cost spikes. If 95p latency > 220ms for 2 consecutive windows, I'll abort and rollback.

jamal_ops: Rollback plan: stop further drains, bring canary nodes back, and redeploy previous driver. We keep image rollback artifacts for 24h.

alex_s: Noted — I'll notify the product owners for any long-running evals. Also, please post customer-facing comms if we hit degraded SLOs.

maria_infra: Post-mortem scope: record time to drain, average eviction time, KV cache warmup delta, and any routing fallbacks. Cost delta (eu-west burst) tracked in the ops-runbook spreadsheet.

jamal_ops: One last thing — please avoid running large embedding jobs from 01:45-05:30 UTC in apac-south. We'll label that window in the quota system.

ops-bot: Reminder set: send 1h and 15m pre-maint alerts.

tony_net: I'll be on-call for net rechecks. If ARP convergence >60s, escalate to network crew.

jamal_ops: Thanks — plan looks green. Will post a short post-maint summary in #eng-infra when we're done. :thumbsup:

sophia_oncall: Thanks team — assigning myself as incident lead for the window.

maria_infra: All right — marking in calendar and updating the runbook with these knobs.
